factors: Eight material claim notes span event semantics, replay, idempotency, authorization and serialization.
The proposed action classifier must separate observed source behavior from unrun tests and uncertain effects.
complexity.rationale: The source is short but the analysis crosses consequential continuation and permission boundaries, so the extended evidence map and counterargument are proportionate.

sourceMap.rationale: The vendor documentation labels a webhook success that can leave a run waiting for human input.
The documented payload and status semantics motivate attribution and UNKNOWN rules as GhostMesh inference.
Vendor replay and idempotency documents inform, but do not prove, separate authorization and destination outcome controls.
The article proposes synthetic callback and state fixtures to falsify an overconfident completion classifier.
Pinned Docling implementation and export materials illustrate the limits of flattening and the need for a bounded comparison.

sourceCoverage.rationale: The five mapped sections identify the pinned webhook documentation and separate supporting references; the original page date and production behavior remain limited.

supportingArgument.rationale: The strongest documented webhook status distinction is represented alongside relevant retry and serialization context without claiming a deployed GhostMesh defect.

evidenceRoles.rationale: Vendor documentation, inspected implementation source, GhostMesh inference and unrun experiments are labeled separately in the claim register.

counterargument.rationale: The article acknowledges that the existing consumer may already handle this correctly and that a new adapter could create competing lifecycle state.

tradeoffs.rationale: It considers the cost of a new orchestration layer against inspecting the incumbent runtime and making the smallest evidence-preserving change.

falsifiability.rationale: Synthetic waiting, duplicate, delayed, missing and completed cases define concrete failures that would reject the proposed reducer.

originalSynthesis.rationale: The GhostMesh thesis distinguishes callback processing, requested outcome, operation identity and permission to perform a consequential action.

performance.rationale: No throughput, latency or accuracy measurement is asserted; the synthetic experiment is framed as a proposed decision-quality test.

economics.rationale: No measured cost claim appears; additional adapter and review effort are acknowledged as a reason to prefer the existing boundary.

threatGovernance.rationale: Authorization, cross-run attribution, uncertain destination effects and replay risk are analyzed as separate control boundaries.

gaps.rationale: Independent review of the exact new article, catalog claims, source map and receipt has not been completed after mechanical presentation changes.
Browser visual and accessibility checks of the generated route have not been completed under the available permitted surface.
The catalog date reflects local draft preparation and must be replaced with the verified first-publication date before production release.

decisionRationale: The approved analysis is preserved, but publication remains held for exact-candidate independent review, visual QA and authenticated owner acceptance on a future PR.
